name: Brent Andersen
bio: Brent Andersen is a Pompano Beach businessman who founded Pilgrim Bay Insurance Agency, a commercial brokerage, in 2010. He previously served two decades on the Massachusetts Republican State Committee, including as treasurer, and on a Massachusetts state finance board. He won the 2026 Republican primary in FL-20 and has not held elected public office.

platform.point: Lower insurance costs by cutting red tape, pursuing tort reform and easing reinsurance treaties.
Backs federal reinsurance solutions and reforms to stabilize Florida's property insurance market.
Supports full funding for local police, school resource officers and community crime prevention.
Would cut federal regulations that raise housing costs and expand paths to homeownership.
Wants more vocational education, apprenticeships and employer partnerships with community colleges.
Would reduce small-business regulation, widen access to capital and support local business incubators.
Asked the White House to grant Deferred Enforced Departure to eligible Venezuelans whose protected status is expiring.
Challenged Rep. Wasserman Schultz to three public debates.

economy.evidence: Proposes cutting red tape, tort reform and fewer regulations on housing and small businesses.

security.evidence: General pledge to fully fund local law enforcement and strengthen school security with resource officers.

immigration.evidence: Pairs a general call for strong borders with a specific request for deportation relief (DED) for eligible Venezuelans.

education.evidence: General statements backing policies that empower parents and defend parental rights.

notes: Searched the campaign site (issues, bio, news), CBS Miami, Coral Springs News and Florida Politics; the Sun Sentinel endorsement says he may accept raising the Social Security wage cap, but that was not scored. No stated positions were found on abortion, guns, foreign policy, energy, tech or religion.

name: Seth Harp
bio: Seth Harp is a seventh-grade civics teacher at Lincoln Middle School in Gainesville. He spent more than 25 years in radio, including as operations manager of ESPN Gainesville, and taught as an adjunct in the University of Florida's journalism college. He won the 2026 Democratic primary in FL-3.

platform.point: Would raise the payroll tax cap to $250,000 to shore up benefits without cutting payments.
Proposes the C.U.B.S. Act with sliding-scale child care subsidies for working families.
Would tax large corporate home purchases at rising rates and reward builders of starter homes.
Would set the corporate tax rate at 26% and cap CEO pay at 150 times median worker pay.
Would cap federal student loan interest at 3.1% and tie repayment to income.
Proposes free universal lunch for every public-school student nationwide.
Would treat broadband as critical infrastructure with a target price of $10 per month.
Aims to double the behavioral health workforce and add full VA dental coverage for veterans.

economy.evidence: Proposes a 26% corporate tax rate, a CEO pay cap, taxes on executive stock awards and escalating taxes on corporate home buying.

welfare.evidence: Backs guaranteed affordable health care, universal school lunch and expanded child care subsidies.

energy.evidence: General plan to invest in water conservation and strengthen freshwater protections; no stated climate or energy policy.

education.evidence: Proposes universal lunch for public-school students and says new revenue should go to education; no stated view on vouchers.

notes: Searched the campaign home, About and Issues pages plus local news (Fox 51, Alligator, WUFT); no questionnaires or debate coverage turned up, and no positions were found on abortion, guns, immigration, foreign policy, AI or religion. Not the same person as former Georgia state senator Seth Harp or the journalist of the same name.

name: LaShonda Holloway
current_role: Former federal official and banking community lending director
bio: LaShonda "L.J." Holloway holds a law degree from the University of Florida, worked for Congresswoman Carrie Meek and held posts at the EPA, and most recently directed community lending at a bank. She has said she is not a licensed attorney. She is the Democratic nominee for Florida's 4th District for the third time.

platform.point: Wants lower premiums and drug costs, expanded Medicare and quality care as a basic right.
Would invest in American clean energy and domestic supply chains to keep energy prices stable.
Would cut red tape, expand access to capital and shield Main Street firms from unfair corporate competition.
Says full-time work should cover food, housing, health care and transportation.
Supports investing in public schools, skilled trades and technology training.
Would fully fund VA health care and expand veterans' mental health and housing services.
Aims to lower rents, add housing supply and help working families buy homes.
Wants every eligible citizen able to vote freely and without barriers.

economy.evidence: General call for a living wage that covers basic costs, alongside cutting red tape for small businesses.

welfare.evidence: Treats health care as a basic right and calls for expanded Medicare coverage and guaranteed access to care.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion bans as a limit on basic rights (abortion), while backing gun regulation (guns).

security.evidence: General support for criminal justice reform listed among the legislation she would back.

foreign.evidence: Criticized reported U.S. military action in Venezuela in January 2026, saying it put Americans at risk.

energy.evidence: General support for investing in American clean energy and for climate action.

education.evidence: General support for investing in strong public school education and lowering college costs.

notes: Searched the campaign platform, about and media pages, Florida Politics primary coverage, Action News Jax and the Westside Gazette; the earlier 'attorney' role was corrected because she told Florida Politics she did not pass the bar. Liberty and security evidence comes from a Westside Gazette profile whose abortion quote may date from an earlier campaign; no positions were found on immigration, AI or religion.

name: Rachel Grage
bio: Rachel Grage is a biomedical engineer who researched cardiac therapies and treatments for children with cerebral palsy, with engineering degrees from Tulane University. She has served as an elected homeowners' association president and was the Democratic nominee for Florida House District 16 in 2024. She won the 2026 Democratic primary in FL-5.

platform.point: Keep health premiums and drug prices affordable, maintain federal cost-sharing aid and stabilize home insurance.
Protect Medicare and Social Security benefits and secure their long-term solvency.
Increase campaign finance transparency and reduce the influence of big money in politics.
Says ICE should be dismantled while keeping some form of federal immigration enforcement.
Protect personal privacy, access to healthcare and equal treatment under the law.
Defend coastal ecosystems, expand conservation funding and invest in disaster resilience.
Opposed the 2025 federal tax law's permanent cuts for top earners and its cuts to IRS enforcement funding.
Supports keeping Florida's school vaccine requirements, with existing exemptions left in place.

economy.evidence: Opposed permanent tax cuts for the wealthiest and cuts to IRS enforcement in the 2025 federal tax law.

welfare.evidence: Opposes Medicaid and food-assistance cuts and pledges to keep federal health cost-sharing aid and protect Medicare and Social Security.

liberty.evidence: Pledges to protect privacy, healthcare access and equal treatment (abortion, LGBTQ) and criticized Florida school book removals (speech).

immigration.evidence: Called for dismantling ICE on WJCT, while her site also backs secure borders through efficient enforcement with due process.

energy.evidence: Criticized the 2025 federal tax law for repealing clean-energy investments and backs conservation funding.

education.evidence: Faulted Florida's education board for focusing on book removals over teacher pay and crowded classrooms; general, no voucher position.

notes: Searched the campaign site, her Substack archive, Florida Politics and Florida Trib coverage; no positions were found on policing, foreign policy, AI or religion. The campaign site does not clearly identify a standalone headshot image.

name: Dan Green
current_role: U.S. Navy Reserve officer and former Pentagon official
bio: Dan Green is a U.S. Navy Reserve commander who joined the Navy after working at the Pentagon on September 11, 2001, and deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan, including with SEAL teams. He also served a civilian State Department tour in Afghanistan and was Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Strategy and Force Development. He narrowly won the 2026 Republican primary in Florida's 9th District.

platform.point: Keep the military well funded and ready.
Bring down homeowners insurance rates for Floridians.
Lower grocery, gas and fuel prices by reversing Biden administration policies.
Address overdevelopment pressures on Central Florida communities.
Strongly favors federal spending cuts through deregulation, less bureaucracy and more oversight.
Strongly agrees the federal Department of Education should be eliminated.
Supports legal protection from conception, with exceptions for rape, incest and the mother's life.
Says current gun laws already impose too many restrictions.

economy.evidence: Questionnaire answers oppose higher taxes and strongly back spending cuts and deregulation.

welfare.evidence: Questionnaire answer favors private health insurance with fiscally limited government assistance.

liberty.evidence: Backs protection from conception (abortion) and one-man-one-woman marriage (LGBTQ), but says gun laws are too restrictive (guns).

immigration.evidence: Questionnaire answers welcome immigrants who use legal channels and strongly oppose sanctuary cities.

foreign.evidence: Pledges strong military funding and, in his questionnaire, backs selective intervention, close ties with Israel and treats China as a threat.

education.evidence: Strongly agrees with eliminating the U.S. Department of Education.

faith.evidence: Strongly opposes requiring people to provide services that violate their religious beliefs, supporting religious exemptions.

photo.author: JoAnne Sorrentino, U.S. Department of Defense

notes: Added scores from his own iVoterGuide questionnaire answers (not the guide's ratings) plus the campaign site; he named nuclear as the most reliable energy source, which was not scored. No stated positions were found on surveillance or policing powers or on tech regulation.

name: John Cowan
bio: Dr. John Cowan is a Bartow County native and neurosurgeon with degrees from Davidson College and Johns Hopkins medical school who has founded several businesses in northwest Georgia. He finished second to Marjorie Taylor Greene in the 2020 GA-14 Republican runoff. He won the 2026 Republican runoff for Georgia's open 11th District.

platform.point: Wants to fix problems he attributes to Obamacare by lowering premiums and expanding patient choice.
Proposes tax relief for families and small businesses and strengthening domestic industries.
Supports proof of citizenship to vote and transparency in ballot counting.
Pledges to protect free speech, freedom of worship and Second Amendment rights.
Supports banning congressional stock trading, stronger ethics rules and term limits.
Said the U.S. cannot tolerate a nuclear-capable or nuclear-seeking Iran.
Cites federal debt and a broken health system as reasons to overhaul Washington.

economy.evidence: Proposes tax relief for families and small businesses; in 2020 also backed tort reform and market-based health insurance.

welfare.evidence: Opposes Obamacare and favors patient choice; in 2020 he backed market-based insurance purchasing.

liberty.evidence: Opposed abortion in a 2020 interview (abortion) but pledges to protect Second Amendment rights (guns) and free speech (speech).

immigration.evidence: In a 2020 campaign ad he pledged to help President Trump build the border wall; no 2026 immigration statement found.

foreign.evidence: At a 2026 Cherokee County forum he said the U.S. cannot accept a nuclear-capable or nuclear-seeking Iran.

faith.evidence: General pledge to protect freedom of worship among constitutional rights.

notes: AJC and East Cobb News confirm he is the same Cowan who ran in GA-14 in 2020, so abortion and immigration evidence comes from that campaign. No positions were found on policing or surveillance, energy, tech or education.

name: James Duffie
bio: James R. "Jim" Duffie is the Republican nominee for Georgia's 4th District and chairs the Georgia GOP's 4th District committee. He lists himself as CEO of Ablelife Biotech and a U.S. Navy veteran. He ran for the Georgia House in 2016.

platform.point: Would replace federal income, payroll, estate and gift taxes with the FairTax and abolish the IRS.
Would cut regulations that make it harder to hire, invest and compete.
Supports law enforcement and policies he says restore accountability.
Calls for a strong military, secure borders and support for veterans.
Pledges to defend constitutional rights, including the Second Amendment.
Backs transparency, fiscal discipline and constitutional limits on federal power.

economy.evidence: Would replace federal income and payroll taxes with the FairTax, abolish the IRS and cut regulations.

liberty.evidence: General pledge to defend Second Amendment rights (guns); no stated views on abortion, drugs, LGBTQ rights or speech.

security.evidence: General statement supporting law enforcement and safe neighborhoods.

immigration.evidence: General statement that America must secure its borders.

notes: His campaign site loads its content with scripts and could not be read directly, so positions come from his own statements quoted on his BallotReady profile; Vote-USA and OpenCampaign had no answers. No positions were found on health care, abortion, energy, tech, schools or religion.

name: John Salvesen
bio: John "Bongo" Salvesen is the Republican nominee for Georgia's 5th Congressional District. Originally from South Jersey, he has lived in Atlanta since 1994 and has run a handyman business since then. He was the Republican nominee for the same seat in 2024, his first run for office.

platform.point: Supports using paper ballots to secure elections.
Pledges to own no stock and accept contributions only from individuals, not companies.
Promises a weekly podcast to report to constituents.
Warns that the Federal Reserve's FedNow system is a tracking tool that could eliminate cash.
Criticizes the FDA and USDA and highlights food additives banned in other countries.

security.evidence: General warning that the FedNow payment system is a tracking program that would eliminate cash.

notes: Read his campaign site (bongo4congress.com: about, health, FedNow, elections and representation pages), BallotReady, Branch and AJC race coverage; most pages link to videos rather than stating policies. No positions were found on taxes, health coverage, abortion, guns, immigration, foreign policy, energy, schools or religion.
